subject: Use INLA to sequentially update the posterior?

messages.author: 12836e6a447153b7
messages.subject: Use INLA to sequentially update the posterior?
parts:
Hi help,
 
I noticed that INLA can do multiple likelihoods, for example given a latent field x,
y_1|x ~ p_1(theta_1) and y_2|x ~ p2(theta2)
Then by using two likelihoods, both y_1 (data set) and y_2 (data set) can be used to update the belief about x.
However, when there are more and more data sets coming into hand, saying y_1, y_2, y_3, ..., y_p, we seem to have to create a p-column matrix responses to use the p likelihoods to do the modelling together... Which seems to be not handy/automatic when p is large, and we have to re-run the model if a new set of data y_{p+1} is available, and the big matrix of responses seem to be very large internally and make the inference process more memory/time consuming I guess?
Hence, is it possible to do sequential updating in INLA? Saying, x|y_1 as prior for y_2|x, x|(y_1,y_2) as prior for y_3|x, and so on...?
 
Thanks a lot!
Ming

Hi,

there is a way to let the posterior for \theta be the prior for \theta
in a new model (control.update)

In the case where you want to update this sequencially, you also need
to update your knowlegde about the latent field. there is no automatic
way of doing this. 

I guess you can do this approximately, but how and how good this is,
depends on the model. We might discuss it more easily if you write some
more details to he...@r-inla.org
